records.claim_text: Controlling Area is a required field on the SAP PS project definition and is inherited by every new WBS element created or inserted into the structure.
records.evidence_quote: Inherited by any new elements your create or insert into the WBS.

records.claim_text: The controlling area on a project definition can only be changed while creating it; after the first save it is frozen (exception: standard WBS).
records.evidence_quote: Yes, but only when you are creating the project definition. Once you have saved, you cannot change the controlling area

records.claim_text: All WBS elements of a project definition, plus its assigned networks and network activities, must belong to the project definition's controlling area.
records.evidence_quote: The WBS elements belonging to a project definition, along with assigned networks and network activities, must be assigned to the controlling area

records.claim_text: Company codes and business areas used on WBS elements, networks and activities must lie inside the controlling area of the project definition or network header.
records.evidence_quote: The company code(s) and business area in the WBS elements, networks, and network activities must be in the controlling area for the project definition

records.claim_text: The company code entered on a WBS element must belong to the controlling area assigned to the project.
records.evidence_quote: The company code must belong to the assigned controlling area.

records.claim_text: Individual WBS elements within one project may carry different company codes, so company code is not uniform across the hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: Different WBS elements can be assigned to different company codes.

records.claim_text: The company code of a WBS element becomes non-changeable once plan values, actual values, commitments or budget exist on it.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot change the company code if plan/actual values, commitments, or budget exist.

records.claim_text: Business area is a required WBS element field only when business area balance sheets are managed in the company code; otherwise it is not mandatory.
records.evidence_quote: Required, if business area balances are managed in the company code.

records.claim_text: The business area on a WBS element cannot be changed once plan or actual values, commitments or budget exist.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot change the business area if plan/actual values, commitments, or budget exist.

records.claim_text: Profit centre is documented as an optional field on both the SAP PS project definition and the WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Profit Center Type of field Optional

records.claim_text: Plant is optional on the WBS element but when entered it must belong to the company code assigned to that WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The plant must belong to the assigned company code.

records.claim_text: If the object currency is left blank on the project definition the system derives it from the company code.
records.evidence_quote: If you do not fill this field, the system copies the company code into it.

records.claim_text: WBS element object currency is changeable only when the controlling area forbids differing company code currencies and no plan/actual, commitment or budget values exist.
records.evidence_quote: Only if the controlling area does not allow different company code currencies and if no plan/actual values, commitments, or budget exist for the WBS element.

records.claim_text: When new WBS elements are created or incorporated into a work breakdown structure, organizational values are copied down from the project definition.
records.evidence_quote: When you create new WBS elements or incorporate them into a WBS, the values from the project definition are copied into the WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Inheritance is a one-time copy: later changes to the project definition do not propagate to WBS elements that already took the value.
records.evidence_quote: the changes have no effect on the values taken from the project definition and inserted into existing WBS elements

records.claim_text: Changing a project profile later has no effect on values already copied from that profile into existing project definitions.
records.evidence_quote: If you make changes to the project profile later, the changes have no effect on the values taken from the project profile

records.claim_text: Object class is a required value for new WBS elements and is defaulted from the project definition on creation.
records.evidence_quote: Object Class Type of field Required value for new WBS elements

records.claim_text: The controlling area and company code of a network header are display-only and are determined by the plant, not entered by the user.
records.evidence_quote: No; determined when the plant is created.

records.claim_text: The plant on an activity-assigned network activity must belong to the controlling area of the network header.
records.evidence_quote: Must belong to the controlling area for the network header.

records.claim_text: A project profile must be entered whenever a work breakdown structure is created; it is not optional.
records.evidence_quote: When you create a work breakdown structure, you must also enter a project profile for the project.

records.claim_text: The project profile carries default values and parameters for the project, including which settlement schema applies.
records.evidence_quote: The project profile contains default values and parameters for processing the project, for example, which settlement schema is valid

records.claim_text: The project profile is stored on the project definition once the WBS is created, and its defaults may then be overridden per object.
records.evidence_quote: If you create a work breakdown structure, the project profile is saved in the project definition.

records.claim_text: In the project profile the Controlling Area default applies only at project definition level and is changeable up to the first save.
records.evidence_quote: Controlling Area (Project Definition): Can be changed up to first SAVE.

records.claim_text: The project profile Organization block defaults company code, business area, plant, functional area and profit centre for both project definition and WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Company Code, Business Area, Plant, Functional Area, & Profile Center (Project Definition & WBS Element):

records.claim_text: Project currency at project definition and WBS element level depends on the controlling area and company code assignment.
records.evidence_quote: Project Currency (Project Definition & WBS Element): Depends on Controlling Area and Company Code

records.claim_text: Settlement profile is a project profile field defaulting at project definition and WBS element level and defines permitted settlement receivers.
records.evidence_quote: Settlement Profile (Project Definition & WBS element): The settlement profile specifies, foe example, the permitted settlement receives for the WBS elements.

records.claim_text: Investment profile is a project profile field at project definition and WBS element level controlling integration with Investment Management.
records.evidence_quote: Investment Profile (Project Definition & WBS element): specifies how the project is integrated with Investment Management.

records.claim_text: Object class must be explicitly assigned in the master record of a WBS element, unlike cost centres which belong to a class automatically.
records.evidence_quote: others need to be explicitly assigned to an object class in their master record

records.claim_text: A WBS element flagged statistical cannot be settled.
records.evidence_quote: A statistical WBS element cannot be settled.

records.claim_text: The settlement rule strategy in the project profile defines the account assignment category, for example the responsible cost centre.
records.evidence_quote: Account assignment category - example: responsible cost center

records.claim_text: For projects the costing sheet used for overhead determination is entered in the project profile.
records.evidence_quote: For projects you enter the costing sheet in the project profile.

records.claim_text: Assigning an investment profile to an order or WBS element is what turns that object into an investment measure.
records.evidence_quote: By assigning an investment profile to an order or WBS element, you make it into an investment measure.

records.claim_text: The investment profile can trigger automatic creation of an accompanying asset under construction when the order or WBS element is released.
records.evidence_quote: Automatic creation of an accompanying asset under construction when the order or WBS element is released

records.claim_text: An indicator in the investment profile decides whether one AuC is created per investment measure or one per source structure assignment.
records.evidence_quote: you control whether the system creates exactly one asset under construction per investment measure, or one asset under construction per assignment in the source structure

records.claim_text: The investment profile is assigned to the project profile on its Controlling tab and flows to the project definition as a default.
records.evidence_quote: You assign the investment profile to the project profile in the Customizing definition of the project profile (on the Controlling tab page).

records.claim_text: The investment profile on the project definition defaults into newly created WBS elements and can be removed manually on non-capitalised elements.
records.evidence_quote: The investment profile specified in the project definition is also used as a default when individual work breakdown structure (WBS) elements are created.

records.claim_text: An indicator in the investment profile decides whether periodic and full settlement of the investment measure is by line item or by totals.
records.evidence_quote: This indicator controls whether the periodic settlement and full settlement of investment measures should be by line item or by totals.

records.claim_text: Asset classes used for investment measures carry a special indicator that reserves them for that purpose.
records.evidence_quote: You set this indicator in the asset class, in order to reserve the asset class for investment measures.

records.claim_text: The system copies company code, business area, requesting cost centre, location and tax jurisdiction code from the WBS element to the generated AuC.
records.evidence_quote: Organizational assignments (company code, business area, requesting cost center, location, tax jurisdiction code)

records.claim_text: Organizational assignment fields on an automatically created AuC cannot be changed in Asset Accounting because they must agree with the WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: the fields that have to agree with the order or WBS element (such as organizational assignments) cannot be changed there.

records.claim_text: The settlement profile defines which receiver types settlement is permitted to, for example cost centres and orders but not fixed assets.
records.evidence_quote: This is where you define which receivers you can settle to.

records.claim_text: The settlement profile determines whether periodic settlement percentage rates must total 100% or may be less than full.
records.evidence_quote: Whether the total of the settlement percentage rates must be 100% during periodic settlement, or whether the total can be less than 100%

records.claim_text: The allocation structure groups primary and secondary cost elements and decides per group whether settlement is by cost element or via a settlement cost element.
records.evidence_quote: For each group, you specify whether (for settlement to a given receiver type) settlement is performed by cost element or using a settlement cost element.

records.claim_text: A source structure groups cost elements into assignments so that a different settlement receiver can be entered per assignment.
records.evidence_quote: When you enter a distribution rule, you can enter a different receiver for each assignment.

records.claim_text: A source structure is unnecessary when all cost elements are settled using the same rules.
records.evidence_quote: You do not need a source structure if you want to settle all your cost elements using the same rules.

records.claim_text: With the To be settled in full setting, closing an object or flagging it for deletion errors out when its balance is not zero.
records.evidence_quote: the system generates an error message if the balance for the object is not zero

records.claim_text: A PA transfer structure is only needed when objects are settled to Profitability Analysis.
records.evidence_quote: The PA transfer structure is only required when you settle objects to Profitability Analysis (CO-PA).

records.claim_text: Settlement rules are stored in the master record of the order or WBS element itself.
records.evidence_quote: You enter the settlement rules in the master record of the order or WBS element.

records.claim_text: Settlement to an asset under construction is carried out using capitalization keys, which allow different percentage rates per depreciation area.
records.evidence_quote: The system settles to the asset under construction using the capitalization key.

records.claim_text: The settlement profile is stored in the project profile or the network type and then acts as the default for individual project objects.
records.evidence_quote: You store the settlement profile in the project profile or in the network type. It then acts as a default value for the individual objects.

records.claim_text: A settlement rule must be maintained in every sender object before a project can be settled.
records.evidence_quote: You must also maintain a settlement rule in each sender before you can settle a project.

records.claim_text: For actual costs the settlement profile sets one of three modes: must be settled in full, can be settled, or must not be settled.
records.evidence_quote: You use the settlement profile to define the following for actual costs: Must be settled in full Can be settled Must not be settled

records.claim_text: In multi-level settlement WBS elements must always be settled to the WBS element directly above them in the hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: You must always settle WBS elements to the element directly above them in the hierarchy.

records.claim_text: Settlement criteria are defined in the project master data rather than only in Customizing.
records.evidence_quote: You define the settlement criteria in the project master data.

records.claim_text: Automatic settlement rule generation can target a profitability segment, the responsible cost centre, the requesting cost centre, the superior object, or no settlement.
records.evidence_quote: Settlement to the responsible cost center Settlement to the requesting cost center Adopting the settlement rule from the superior object No settlement

records.claim_text: Automatic settlement rule generation requires a strategy defined both in Project System Customizing and in the project profile in use.
records.evidence_quote: You must also define a strategy in the project profile you are using.

records.claim_text: Automatic settlement rule generation is not available for capital-investment projects.
records.evidence_quote: Automatic settlement rule generation is not available for capital-investment projects.

records.claim_text: Rule generation writes the settlement profile, results analysis key and settlement rule into the WBS element master data.
records.evidence_quote: The settlement profile for the WBS element This determines, for example, which receivers are allowed for settlement

records.claim_text: In SAP S/4HANA Cloud the profit centre and functional area of a billing element are identical for every WBS element in its subtree.
records.evidence_quote: The Profit Center and Functional Area of a Billing Element is same for all the WBS elements in its subtree structure.

records.claim_text: Settlement rules cannot be entered on WBS elements that sit inside a billing element subtree.
records.evidence_quote: you will not be able to enter any settlement rule on the WBS elements in the billing element subtree

records.claim_text: When a WBS element is created, included or indented below a billing element the functional area and profit centre are adjusted automatically.
records.evidence_quote: All the WBS elements in the subtree of a billing element must have the same functional area and profit center as the billing element.

records.claim_text: In cloud revenue projects, cost centres inside one billing element hierarchy must belong to the same company code, though child WBS elements may otherwise differ.
records.evidence_quote: Make sure that you maintain cost centers that belong to the same company code iin the same billing element hierarchy.

records.claim_text: A newly created cloud WBS element derives its organizational assignments and control parameters such as costing sheet and investment profile from the project header.
records.evidence_quote: It derives the following values from the project header: the organizational assignments of the WBS element

records.claim_text: The cloud WBS Element app exposes organizational assignments of a WBS element such as cost centre, plant and tax jurisdiction for editing.
records.evidence_quote: Edit the organizational assignments of the WBS element, such as cost center, plant, and tax jurisdiction.

records.claim_text: In an overhead project profile, period-end closing generates settlement rules to the responsible cost centre and then settles the costs.
records.evidence_quote: generate settlement rules to the responsible cost center and finally settle the costs, based on your requirement

records.claim_text: In SAP S/4HANA Cloud the investment profile is explicitly not a mandatory field on an investment project.
records.evidence_quote: The investment profile, however, is not a mandatory field.

records.claim_text: Assigning an investment profile and releasing the WBS element generates the asset under construction; costs can settle to multiple AuCs via source structure.
records.evidence_quote: By assigning an investment profile to the project or WBS element and upon releasing the WBS element, the asset under construction is generated.

records.claim_text: For a statistical cloud project the statistical flag applies to all WBS elements in the hierarchy and a default cost centre must be set per WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: At the WBS element level, you must set the cost center to which the costs are actually posted by default.

records.claim_text: Statistical WBS elements can neither be settled nor carry overhead.
records.evidence_quote: Statistical WBS elements cannot be settled or carry overheads.

records.claim_text: A revenue project may hold different responsible cost centres, profit centres and functional area values within the same company code.
records.evidence_quote: There can be different responsible cost centers, profit center and functional area values associated with the same company code.

records.claim_text: A project can carry only one project profile.
records.evidence_quote: There can only be one project profile per project.

records.claim_text: Project authorization restrictions are defined over controlling area, company code, cost centre, profit centre, plant, functional area, project profile and project type.
records.evidence_quote: grant access to all projects and WBS elements of a specified controlling area, company code, cost center, profit center, plant, functional area, project profile

records.claim_text: Business area is an external accounting organizational unit corresponding to a business segment or area of responsibility.
records.evidence_quote: Organizational unit of external accounting that corresponds to a specific business segment or area of responsibility in a company.

records.claim_text: Defining the business area organizational unit is optional in SAP.
records.evidence_quote: The definition of the business area organizational unit is optional

records.claim_text: Business area can be derived at posting time from other account assignments such as the cost centre master record.
records.evidence_quote: the business area can also be derived from other account assignments, such as the cost center

records.claim_text: A functional area is an account assignment characteristic that sorts operating expenses by function such as production, administration or sales.
records.evidence_quote: A functional area is an account assignment characteristic that sorts operating expenses according to functions.

records.claim_text: Cost of sales accounting obliges the enterprise to sort operating expenses by functional area.
records.evidence_quote: If you use cost of sales accounting, you have to sort your operating expenses by functional area.

records.claim_text: Functional area can be entered in the master data of the project profile, project definition and WBS element among other objects.
records.evidence_quote: Project profile and project definition

records.claim_text: The functional area field is only ready for input when cost of sales accounting is active or active for preparation for the company code.
records.evidence_quote: cost of sales accounting for your company codes must either be active for preparation or active

records.claim_text: Once postings exist against an object, its functional area can no longer be changed.
records.evidence_quote: Where postings already exist, it is no longer possible to change the functional area.

records.claim_text: A segment is a division of a company for which external financial statements can be produced.
records.evidence_quote: Division of a company for which you can create financial statements for external reporting.

records.claim_text: The segment characteristic is only released together with the profit centre characteristic.
records.evidence_quote: The characteristic Segment is only released in combination with the characteristic Profit Center

records.claim_text: If no segment is entered manually at posting, the segment is determined from the master record of the profit centre.
records.evidence_quote: the segment is determined from the master record of the profit center

records.claim_text: The controlling area to company code relationship may be 1:1 or 1:n and is very hard to change once assigned.
records.evidence_quote: It is difficult or at best, time-consuming to change the 1:1 or 1:n relationsip between the controlling area and company code

records.claim_text: Assigning several company codes to one controlling area requires a consistent chart of accounts across those company codes.
records.evidence_quote: You need to use a consistent chart of accounts

records.claim_text: The operative fiscal year variants of the company codes must match the fiscal year variant of the controlling area.
records.evidence_quote: The operative fiscal year variants in the company codes must match the fiscal year variants in the controlling area.

records.claim_text: Direct settlement sends each project object straight to an external cost object such as a cost centre or profitability segment.
records.evidence_quote: Each object is settled directly to the external cost object (examples: cost center, profitability segment).

records.claim_text: For open item settlement of an asset under construction a settlement profile must be assigned to the company codes involved.
records.evidence_quote: for open item settlement, you have to assign a settlement profile to the company codes involved

records.claim_text: Capitalisable parts of an AuC must settle to capitalised assets while non-capitalisable parts may settle as adjustment postings to cost centres.
records.evidence_quote: You must settle those parts of the asset under construction that require capitalization to capitalized assets.

records.claim_text: Only acquisitions from the current fiscal year may be settled from an AuC to CO receivers.
records.evidence_quote: you can only settle acquisitions from the current fiscal year to CO receivers

records.claim_text: SAP training material groups the project profile organizational data as controlling area, company code and business area.
records.evidence_quote: Controlling area, Company code, Business area

records.claim_text: The settlement profile specifies whether settlement is allowed and which allocation structure and PA transfer structure are used.
records.evidence_quote: You specify in the settlement profile whether settlement is allowed, which receivers are allowed for settlement

records.claim_text: A source structure is defined when costs must settle to different receivers depending on the cost element.
records.evidence_quote: You define a source structure if you want to settle the costs incurred for the order to different receivers depending on the cost element.

records.claim_text: Inference: the mandatory PS accounting spine is controlling area plus company code plus object currency plus object class; business area is conditional and profit centre, plant, functional area optional.
records.evidence_quote: Required, if business area balances are managed in the company code.

records.claim_text: Inference: settlement behaviour is driven by settlement profile (permitted receivers), allocation structure (settlement cost element), source structure (receiver split) and investment profile (AuC and line-item mode).
records.evidence_quote: The settlement process is controlled using various parameters, including: Settlement Profile Allocation Structure PA Transfer Structure Source Structure

records.claim_text: Inference: PS inheritance is copy-on-create from project profile to project definition to WBS element, not a live reference, so downstream systems must replicate snapshot semantics.
records.evidence_quote: The values for the project definition are copied from the template or project profile when you create a work breakdown structure.
